title: Outlook: new settings to block or load external images
summary: Hold: the page labels the new control off by default without evidence and calls licensing unknown despite Microsoft's published Outlook licensing requirements. Its roadmap facts match the record, and targeted searches did not locate the new admin allowance, but its tenant-wide scope is not established.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft's deployment guidance says junk senders add web beacons containing external content such as graphic images.
claims.quote: Junk email senders often add a web beacon in HTML email messages that includes external content, such as graphic images.

claims.claim: Opening or viewing a message containing a web beacon can confirm that the email address is valid.
claims.quote: When users open or view the email, the web beacons verify that their email addresses are valid.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no change to sign-in, roles or identity.
claims.quote: New settings will allow customers to block all external content, or to load all content by default if the customer admin allows. Existing default behavior will not be changed (load external content only for safe senders).

claims.claim: The roadmap describes external-image display settings rather than an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Outlook on the web and the new Outlook for Windows now support will support new settings for loading external images.

claims.claim: ExternalImageProxyEnabled controls whether external images load through the Outlook external image proxy.
claims.quote: The ExternalImageProxyEnabled parameter specifies whether to load all external images through the Outlook external image proxy.

claims.claim: The proxy parameter is not documented as the block-all or load-all-by-default allowance.
claims.quote:
$true: All external images are loaded through the Outlook external image proxy. This value is the default.
- $false: All external images are loaded through the web browser.

claims.claim: By default users can configure their own safelist collection in Outlook or Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: By default, users can configure the safelist collection on their own mailboxes in Outlook or Outlook on the web.

claims.claim: Admins can configure a user's safelist collection with Set-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration.
claims.quote: Admins can use the corresponding parameters on the Set-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration cmdlet to configure the safelist collection on a user's mailbox.

claims.claim: Under the roadmap's stated default, safe-sender status determines which senders' external content loads.
claims.quote: Existing default behavior will not be changed (load external content only for safe senders).

claims.claim: The planned load-all option extends external-content loading beyond safe senders.
claims.quote: or to load all content by default if the customer admin allows. Existing default behavior will not be changed (load external content only for safe senders).
